Title: Tempered Shortcut Learning & Structured Artifact Detection
Reported_Claim: ForensicNet detects genuine re-watermarking artifacts rather than simple image distortion shortcuts. Handcrafted residual/spectral baselines fail (LR AUC 0.5569, RF AUC 0.5500).
Scientific_Qualification: Perturbation strength contributes modestly (+0.075 AUC over chance), but structured multi-embedding interference provides the dominant signal (AUC 0.730 vs. noise-matched, 0.854 vs. single watermark controls). Claims of zero energy shortcut must be qualified.
Key_Empirical_Metrics: LR AUC: 0.5569; RF AUC: 0.5500; Strength-matched AUC: 0.5747; Matched-noise AUC: 0.7296; Primary AUC: 0.8543

Title: Decisive Superiority over Handcrafted Forensic Baselines
Reported_Claim: RW-Guard significantly and decisively outperforms handcrafted residual and spectral baseline models on identical held-out evaluation sources.
Scientific_Qualification: None. Fully paired source-level bootstrap comparison definitively confirms statistical superiority.
Key_Empirical_Metrics: RW-Guard 500 AUC: 0.8477; Delta vs LR: +0.2908 (p < 0.001); Delta vs RF: +0.2982 (p < 0.001)

Title: TrustMark Generalization & Domain-Recalibrated Adaptation
Reported_Claim: RW-Guard generalizes to unseen deep neural watermarking architectures (TrustMark).
Scientific_Qualification: Uncalibrated zero-shot detection rate at frozen threshold is ineffective (0.0% TPR) due to domain score shift, despite ranking discriminability (0.6562 AUC). Effective detection on TrustMark requires either threshold recalibration (tau = 0.170 -> 22.0% TPR) or 15% supervised adaptation (AUC 0.8505).
Key_Empirical_Metrics: Zero-shot AUC: 0.6562; Zero-shot TPR(tau): 0.0%; Recalibrated TPR: 22.0%; 15% Adapted AUC: 0.8505

Title: StegaStamp Zero-Shot Forensic Detection
Reported_Claim: RW-Guard exhibits strong zero-shot forensic detection on StegaStamp deep watermarked images without retraining.
Scientific_Qualification: High ranking capability (AUC 0.9293) confirms strong forensic sensitivity to deep spatial perturbations, though fixed-threshold sensitivity is modest (5.33%) without domain threshold adjustment.
Key_Empirical_Metrics: StegaStamp AUC: 0.9293; TPR@1%FPR: 0.1667; Fixed TPR(tau): 0.0533; Fixed FPR(tau): 0.0067

Title: Dual Watermark Survival Dominates Overwriting Attacks
Reported_Claim: Second-generation watermarking attacks do not obliterate original watermarks; dual survival is the dominant physical outcome.
Scientific_Qualification: None. Empirical recovery logs strictly confirm 85.0% dual survival, refuting the naive assumption that second-watermark insertion erases previous ownership marks.
Key_Empirical_Metrics: Dual Survival: 85.0% (425/500); Overwrite: 13.4% (67/500); Attacker Fail: 1.6% (8/500); Both Fail: 0.0%

Title: Vulnerability to Gradient-Based Adversarial Perturbation
Reported_Claim: Standard ForensicNet models are highly vulnerable to adversarial evasion attacks (PGD-10) without adversarial training.
Scientific_Qualification: None. Confirms that like standard forensic convolutional architectures, RW-Guard requires dedicated adversarial defense in malicious threat models.
Key_Empirical_Metrics: Clean Detection: 36.0%; PGD-10 eps=0.5: 0.0%; PGD-10 eps=1.0: 0.0%; PGD-10 eps=2.0: 0.0%

Title: Validation vs. Test FPR Discrepancy Stemming from Tail Quantization
Reported_Claim: The shift from 1.00% validation FPR to 3.33% test FPR at tau = 1.3394 is due to finite-sample extreme tail variance, not distribution shift.
Scientific_Qualification: Statistical tests conclusively demonstrate that underlying negative score distributions are identical (p = 0.55), but high tail density renders fixed score thresholds sensitive to sample quantization.
Key_Empirical_Metrics: Val FPR: 1.00% (3/300); Test FPR: 3.33% (50/1500); KS test p-value: 0.5485; Mann-Whitney p-value: 0.8658

Title: Multi-Seed Architecture Optimization Stability
Reported_Claim: The seven-scheme ForensicNet architecture and training pipeline converge stably across random seeds.
Scientific_Qualification: None. Very low variance (std = 0.0024) demonstrates reproducible optimization across different parameter initializations.
